rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Long-running prompts stream progress — never go silent.

All three walk-down prompts (push-back-on-the-plan-2, -2-askuserquestion, -2-original, raw L57/L72/L85) tell Claude to read the codebase instead of asking when it can ("If a question can be answered by reading the codebase, read the codebase instead of asking me"), which is precisely the fallback that produced the logged 13-minute silent turn. The exercise's overall Q&A IS interactive, but that doesn't cover a single fallback-triggered turn running 10+ minutes with nothing shown — the student is attending (not a walk-away-by-design case, so §43's carve-out doesn't apply), and none of the three fences carries an in-fence progress-narration instruction. The adjacent 'If it feels slow, ask why' callout (raw L59) is the reactive/recovery half (check_pedagogy.md §48's territory) and doesn't substitute for the proactive streaming habit this rule asks for. Note: the sibling technical-class instance for this file carries a stale carried-forward N/A on this exact rule (reasoning: 'not a silent multi-minute unattended run') that does not engage with this dry-run evidence; flagged in this instance's top-level `notes`.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Two distinct self-report-inflation instances live in this file. (1) Phase-3 plan-regeneration: raw L48's 'read the flagged steps in the revised plan, not the agent's report of them' is a direct verify-at-artifact instruction — well covered (pedagogy.json §31 already confirms this instance PASS; deferred here, not re-derived). (2) Phase-5 push-back-on-the-plan-3 (raw L101): 'what new information and decisions did the second-pass read surface that my two push-backs didn't?' asks Claude to characterize the VALUE of a run it just performed, inviting self-serving inflation of the walk-down's contribution. The evidence-backed-Debrief carve-out this class recognizes needs the fence to require artifact-level reporting or nearby body prose to name the charity risk with a pushback move; the current 'Compare what each read caught' section right after the fence (raw L103-107) states a comparison RUBRIC (what a human catches vs. what the agent catches) but does not ask the student to check Claude's claim against a specific plan-file line or quote, and does not name the self-serving-inflation risk with a recovery move. A dated maintainer note (raw L123) confirms the value-claim was deliberately relocated to this Compare beat in a 2026-08-02/2026-08-12 rewrite sequence — plausibly the point at which a stronger concrete-evidence anchor (of the kind rule 31(a) asks for) was traded away for narrative placement.
